texts: On day 365 of Year 2, Coraline Ash inherited the Harbor Station.
Coraline Ash wrote her own log every night.
Pell took an apprentice named Roben.
Roben came from a Keeper family.
Pell carried the role of senior Keeper with ease.

q1_issues.issue: (Member sk_role_1 senior_keeper) types the role witness as itself a senior keeper, but "the role of senior Keeper" names what the role is rather than making the role an instance of that person-kind.

q2_gaps: An appositive / naming of-phrase ("the role of senior Keeper"): the genitive rules cover possession, part-whole and a nominalization's object, but not an of-phrase that names the head noun's content.
A past-tense habitual ("wrote her own log every night"): the frequency rule says the event stays unmarked while the tense rule puts (Past e) on any finite past clause, and nothing says which wins.
A manner PP ("with ease"): Manner is specified over how-adverbs, and the "with"-phrase split only separates CoAgent from Instrument, so a manner PP has no defined slot or filler form.

A day-of-year ordinal date ("on day 365 of Year 2"): the calendar term set pairs (Day n) with (Month ...) as a day-of-month, so a bare day-of-year ordinal is stored indistinguishably from a day-of-month.
The emphatic possessive "her own": no carrier for the contrastive component, leaving only the plain Possession link.
review.notes: Names, the Kestrel-River handling of "the Harbor Station", the senior_keeper and keeper_family decompositions, and the every-night slot-plus-cycle pair are correct. "Roben came from a Keeper family" taking Experiencer (a stative origin rather than motion) is a defensible reading of an unlisted case.

issues.reason: (Member sk_role_1 senior_keeper) is false and ill-typed: it makes the role witness an instance of the person-kind senior_keeper (the same witness the parse already types (Member sk_role_1 role)), whereas the text only names which office the role is, so the atom asserts something no words put there (Core patterns).

gaps_confirmed: A naming of-phrase whose complement states the head noun's content ("the role of senior Keeper"): the genitive routes cover possession, part-whole and a nominalization's object, none of which is an office-naming complement.
Past-tense habitual ("wrote her own log every night"): Frequency & habitual schedules says the event stays unmarked, Status predicates puts (Past e) on a finite past clause, and nothing arbitrates.
Manner PP ("with ease"): Manner is specified over how-adverbs only, and the "with"-phrase test splits solely CoAgent from Instrument, so a manner PP has no stated slot or filler form.

Day-of-year ordinal dating ("on day 365 of Year 2"): (Day n) is defined as the day granularity of a calendar expression alongside (Month ...), so a day numbered within the year stores indistinguishably from a day-of-month.
Emphatic possessive "her own": no carrier for the contrastive component beyond the plain Possession link.
new_gaps: Even the nearest licensed carrier for "the role of senior Keeper" — the true-relational-noun genitive (Possession sk_role_1 senior_keeper) — is opaque loose association, so the identity between the role and the office it names is unencodable; a licensed form would need to say that the role IS the senior-Keeper office, not merely that the two are linked.
adjudication.defect_summary: The compliant form drops (Member sk_role_1 senior_keeper), keeps (Member sk_role_1 role) plus the senior_keeper genus/modifier decomposition, and attaches the of-phrase by the true-relational-noun genitive of Complements of nouns and adjectives — the opaque (Possession sk_role_1 senior_keeper) — which records the link without typing the role as a person; no licensed head records the naming/identity relation itself (filed in new_gaps).
adjudication.notes: Everything else holds up: the Harbor Station name+kind pair, the senior_keeper and keeper_family decompositions with the noun modifier correctly unexposed, the every-night slot + (Every e 1 day) cycle pair, and Experiencer on the stative "came from". (Manner sk_carry_1 ease) with a noun filler is graceful improvisation in gap territory — the atom is true of the clause — not a defect.
